overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance for FACTVERSE shows a decisive dominance by high-concept space and astronomy topics, specifically 'What If' planetary scenarios and extreme cosmic anomalies. Videos focusing on surreal planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice, extreme dark worlds) significantly outperform general biological trivia or standard psychological facts in views-per-day and engagement metrics like likes-per-view.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like IYuce8vaU3Y ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') and 8KEl0_pJ_68 ('What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') garnered over 970-1,000+ views with high like-to-view ratios compared to older, static fact listings.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios using sensory-rich, counterintuitive planetary hazards.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Anomalies & Rare Material Weather
winning_patterns.evidence: QXuqYERlqSo ('This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') and v1rrcZLdp4U ('The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b') achieved rapid velocity over 700-1,000 views, showing strong viewer retention affinity for bizarre physical laws in space.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing extreme weather and bizarre material phenomena on newly discovered exoplanets not yet covered on the channel.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 5AN7LUgqarc ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and AXAfwrzzEdU ('Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') stagnated between 50-180 lifetime views with near-zero comments and minimal engagement momentum.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic psychological life hacks and common biology trivia unless paired with a highly counterintuitive, cinematic survival hook.
